title: Bias of the projected sample
statement: Let $n,a,b,s$ be integers with $n>0$, $a>0$, $2a\le b$, and $s\ge1$. Set $\varepsilon=a/b$, and let $J$ be any subset of the $n$ coordinates. Choose uniformly an index from the sample specified by the restricted-weight input with dimension $n$, target bias $\varepsilon$, and Fourier bound $s$, and project the resulting binary vector onto the coordinates outside $J$. Every nonzero Fourier coefficient of the resulting distribution has absolute value at most $\varepsilon/(4s^2)$.
hypotheses_covered: Twice the bias numerator is at most its denominator
Fourier bound $s$ is at least one
$J$ is a subset of the $n$ coordinates
